To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PI3K pathway is a promising target for theranostics of cancers.
the PI3K pathway plays a crucial role in chemoresistance in cancer and the molecular imaging of PI3k pathway is the key to the development of new therapeutics.
the molecular imaging of PI3k/Akt/mTOR signaling axis can be used for the diagnosis and treatment of cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of non-invasive molecular probes and imaging techniques that could be utilized for the detection of PI3K/mTOR pathway in various cancer types and for monitoring the response to PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway inhibitors.
the development of non-invasive molecular probes for imaging PI3K pathway and its components for the purpose of diagnosis of cancer.
the development of non-invasive imaging techniques for the diagnosis and theranostics of PI3K based drug development venture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
non-invasive molecular and functional imaging of PI3k signalling axis is the future of personalized cancer treatment.
non-invasive imaging of the PI3K pathway can be an effective tool to monitor the disease progression and therapeutic response in cancer patients.
non-invasive molecular imagings are the future of PIK3/Akt/mTOR axis based therapeutics and diagnostics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the non-invasive imaging of this pathway would be a great help in the diagnosis, prognosis, prediction of treatment response, monitoring of therapy as well as for the development of new therapeutic strategies.

, the non-invasive imaging of molecular targets in PI3K signalling pathway could be an efficient way to monitor the efficacy of the PI3K inhibitors in preclinical and clinical settings and also for diagnosis and prognosis of cancer.
the non-invasive imaging of this pathway would not only help to monitor the disease but also to monitor the therapeutic response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the PI3k/Akt/mTOR axis can be used as an imaging biomarker and a potential therapeutic target to combat cancer.
the non-invasive molecular approaches should be used in tandem with the conventional techniques to achieve a more accurate, sensitive and specific diagnosis of cancer.
non-invasive imaging can be used to validate the molecular components of PI3K axis for diagnosis of cancer and also for monitoring the therapeutic intervention.
